issues.legal_issue: A managing trustee in whom trust property is legally vested may qualify as a landlord entitled to seek possession of trust land for personal cultivation.
material_facts: The appellant was the managing trustee of a public charitable trust that maintained a dharamshala.
The trust property, including the land in dispute, was legally vested in the appellant as trustee.
The appellant sought possession of land from its tenant on the ground that he intended to cultivate it personally.
The appellant had given the required notice, and the other factual requirements for possession had been decided in his favour.
issues.conclusion: The managing trustee was a landlord entitled to seek surrender of the land for personal cultivation. The appeal was allowed, and the order granting possession to the appellant was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(18) of the Bombay Public Trusts Act, a trustee includes a person in whom trust property is vested. Under sections 2(12) and 2(32) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands (Vidarbha Region) Act, 1958, a trustee in whom the property is vested may be a landlord and may cultivate personally by own labour or under personal supervision using hired labour or servants; such cultivation is on the trustee’s own account. The requirements of section 38(1), read with section 2(12), were therefore satisfied, supporting the possession application under section 36(1). Shri Kalanka Devi Sansthan, Patur v. Pandu Maroti was referred to; Buvasaheb v. Yesu Krishna and Kesheoraj Deo Sansthan, Karanja v. Bapurao were distinguished because they concerned property vested in a deity or juristic person, rather than in a trustee. The Court expressed no opinion on whether a manager or shebait of such property could apply for possession.

predicates.tenancy_possession_claim_for_personal_cu: A claimant sought possession of tenanted land on the ground that it was required for personal cultivation.
predicates.trust_property_legally_vested_in_claiman: The land belonged to a trust and was legally vested in the claimant in the capacity of trustee.
predicates.claimant_is_landlord: The claimant was the landlord of the tenant from whom possession was sought.
predicates.claimant_will_cultivate_by_own_labour_or: The claimant intended to cultivate the land through the claimant’s own labour or under the claimant’s personal supervision using hired labour or servants.

issues.definition: When a trustee seeks possession of tenanted trust land for personal cultivation, the property is legally vested in the trustee, the trustee is the landlord, and the trustee will cultivate it by own labour or personal supervision, the trustee may seek possession for personal cultivation.
